data.title: Borsa Istanbul Activates Circuit Breaker in OTTO.E Shares
data.description:
OTTO HOLDING A.S ( (TR:OTTO) ) has issued an announcement.

Borsa Istanbul has halted continuous trading in OTTO.E shares and shifted the stock to a single-price call auction order collection process. This move activates the exchange’s equity-based circuit breaker mechanism in response to market conditions affecting the company’s shares.

Under the circuit breaker, order collection for OTTO.E will be merged with the closing auction phase, and all matching will occur during the closing auction session. The measure aims to stabilize trading in the stock and ensure more orderly price formation for investors and other market participants.

data.title: Reliance Global Group Amends Credit Deal for Flexibility
data.description:

On September 4, 2026, Reliance Global Group’s subsidiaries entered a Sixth Amendment to their Master Credit Agreement with Oak Street Funding, allowing the approved sale of Southwestern Montana Insurance Center while reallocating only half of the $1.21 million in proceeds to a specified term loan. The change relaxes a prior requirement that all asset sale proceeds be used for debt repayment, enabling Reliance to retain the remaining cash, while Oak Street agreed to release SMI as a borrower and lift its liens on SMI’s assets following the loan paydown, with all guarantors reaffirming their guarantees and waiving related claims.

The amendment, effective upon customary conditions including a $15,000 fee, marks a notable adjustment in Reliance Global Group’s financing structure, providing added liquidity and operational flexibility as it reshapes its portfolio of insurance subsidiaries. data.title: SEALSQ Posts Surging H1 2026 Revenue But Deeper Losses as Post-Quantum Investments Accelerate
data.description:
SEALSQ Corp ( (LAES) ) has shared an update.

On September 11, 2026, SEALSQ reported its financial and operational results for the six months ended June 30, 2026, highlighting sharp revenue growth alongside wider losses. Revenue rose 131% year-on-year to $11.2 million, gross profit jumped 233% to $5.4 million with margins near 48%, but operating loss widened to $32.2 million and net loss to $27.8 million as spending ramped.

Management attributed the top-line gains to renewed demand for Vault-IC secure elements, growth in PKI subscriptions and digital identity services, initial Quantix Edge Security revenue in Spain, and six months of IC’Alps consolidation. IC’Alps added about $2.5 million in sales and broadened the group’s custom ASIC design and secure semiconductor capabilities, while North America accounted for half of first-half revenue, underscoring the region’s importance.
